turns.t: So, um, I had the ultrasound last month, and the report said something about my liver. I wasn't sure what to...
Okay, take your time. Let's start with what the report said. Do you have it with you?
Right here. It says, uh, fatty liver. Mild. And I've been kind of freaking out since.
I understand. Fat in the liver is quite common, and mild is the reassuring word there. Your family doctor sent you to talk through your medicines, right?
Yeah. She said the liver can be affected by, you know, tablets. So I brought the list.
Good thinking. We'll go through each. First, how have you been feeling? Any symptoms?
Not much. Some mild discomfort on my right side, under the ribs. Sometimes. It's, um, more of a nagging than a pain.
A nagging discomfort under the right ribs. How often?
A couple of times a week? After big meals, I guess. I haven't really...
That's okay. You haven't noticed it anywhere else?
No. Just there.
Have you noticed your eyes or skin looking yellow?
No, no yellow. My wife would have said something, she notices everything.
Good. Now the medicines. What's the first one on your list?
Metformin. 500 mg, twice a day, with meals. For my diabetes.
Metformin, 500 mg twice a day, for the diabetes. Which type of diabetes?
Type 2. Diagnosed about six years ago.
Thanks. Next?
Atorvastatin. 20 mg, at bedtime. It's for, uh, cholesterol. I've had high cholesterol for a long time.
Atorvastatin, 20 mg at bedtime, for your cholesterol. Any muscle aches with that?
I don't think so. Hmm, maybe my calves sometimes, but I don't know if that's the...
We'll keep an eye on that. What else?
Lisinopril, 10 mg. Once a day, in the morning. For blood pressure.
Lisinopril, 10 mg once a day for blood pressure. Is that all?
Oh, and the baby aspirin. 81 mg. My cardiologist, um, a few years ago... Anyway, I take it every morning too.
Aspirin, 81 mg every morning. So four medicines in total. Anything over the counter? Supplements?
Nothing else. I'm kind of scared to take anything extra now, because of the liver.
That's sensible. Just check with us or the pharmacist before you add anything new.
Okay, I will.
Is there anything in the family I should know about? Liver trouble, or other illness?
My father had diabetes too. He had it for a long time.
Okay, thank you. Let me have a quick feel of your tummy.
Your abdomen is soft, and I can't feel anything unusual under the ribs on the right.
That's a relief. I was afraid you'd find a lump or something.
Not at all. Let me also read your numbers. Blood pressure is 134 over 82, and weight is 94 kilograms.
The weight's gone up a little. I know. I'm, um...
It happens. Let me say back what I'm hearing. Mild fatty liver on the scan, a nagging right-sided discomfort now and then, and four regular medicines.
Yes, that's it.
Those four medicines are all well-established, and none is a common cause of fatty liver. I'd like to order liver blood tests to see how your liver is working.
Okay. Like, regular blood work?
Yes, a simple blood draw. You can do it at the lab on your way out.
And what should I do about the fat? Is there a pill for it?
Not really. Gradual weight loss, regular movement, and cutting back on sugary drinks help the most. Even a small loss makes a difference.
I can try that. I just... I'm not sure where to start.
Start small. Swap one sugary drink a day for water, and add a ten-minute walk after dinner.
Okay. Water and a walk. I can do that.
Exactly. I'd like to see you again in three months, so we can look at the blood results and how things are going.
Three months. Okay. Thank you. I feel a lot calmer now.
You did well to come in, and bring the list. See you then.
